It addresses the stated issue comprehensively.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The base should fail: (1) test_anthropic_stream_engine_owns_provider_stream_state asserts old files don't exist and new streaming/ files exist—both false in the base; (2) all test imports reference core.anthropic.streaming which doesn't exist in the base; (3) all class references use new names (AnthropicStreamLedger etc.) that don't exist in the base. The gold patch should pass all tests since it implements the exact structure and names the tests check for.

summary: The instance describes a large streaming-layer refactoring. The gold patch is comprehensive and correct for the issue. However, the tests are heavily coupled to the gold patch's specific implementation choices rather than observable behavior. The structural test (test_anthropic_stream_engine_owns_provider_stream_state) requires exact internal module filenames (emitter.py, ledger.py, lifecycle.py, recovery.py) not specified in the issue. Mock patches reference exact internal module paths. Tests import and assert on many implementation-detail names (RecoveryController, TruncatedProviderStreamError, make_text_recovery_body, etc.) beyond what the issue specifies. A valid alternative implementation using the correct public API and package path but different internal module decomposition would fail. Recommend relaxing the structural test to only check the package path and public API exports, and decoupling tests from internal module names.
